name: Gymnema
short: Cited safety data are limited; a 3-month trial reported mainly gastrointestinal effects. A report of two fatal cases of hepatitis with aplastic anaemia names gymnema and homeopathic remedies together.
text: The cited sources give only limited safety information on gymnema (Gymnema sylvestre). In a 3-month randomised comparison with berberine in 50 adults with obesity, which had no placebo group, the most frequent adverse effects in both groups were gastrointestinal symptoms that eased during the first month, and the authors described the side effects of gymnema as minimal; the same trial reported lower fasting glucose with gymnema, but the abstract does not report hypoglycaemia as an adverse event. Case reports describe two patients with hepatitis followed by bone marrow failure (aplastic anaemia), fatal in both; the report's title names gymnema together with homeopathic remedies and its abstract attributes the cases to ayurvedic herbal and homeopathic remedies, so gymnema's own contribution cannot be separated. In a study in rats, a gymnema extract given for 7 days raised blood levels of phenacetin (a test drug for the liver enzyme CYP1A2) and lowered blood levels of tolbutamide (a test drug for CYP2C9), while amlodipine (the test drug for CYP3A4) was not significantly affected; the authors concluded that taking gymnema with medicines metabolised by CYP2C9 and CYP1A2 could lead to interactions. This is animal data, and no interaction data in humans were found in the cited sources.
